newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK gold ends up on late European buying.
newsitem.headline: HK gold ends up on late European buying.

text.p: Hong Kong gold ended up on Thursday from New York's previous close as European customers went on a buying spree shortly before the end of the session, dealers said.
"People were amazed that nothing had happened right after lunch and now there's strong buying," said one source.
The market bounced up in afternoon trade as relatively heavy European buying from commission houses, which serve the public, kicked in later in the afternoon.
"It's options-related buying," said one bullion dealer.
Bullion ended at US$352.10/60 an ounce against New York's US$351.80/352.20 close on Wednesday.
Physical demand remained sidelined on continued expectations the market would dip, bullion dealers said.
"But I think it'll test higher," said one trader, noting good support at $352 per ounce.
Local gold ended HK$29 higher at HK$3,261 a tael.
The carryover charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society rose to -3.90 from its previous fix at -4.50.
